evidence.reason: The run acquires the admission hold (line 773) and enforces ownership before stopping triggers (line 809: require(self.hold.owns(), ...)), but after the service/queue drains and recheck_baseline, it calls self.helper.switch at lines 785-786 without rechecking self.hold.owns(); the hold is only released later at line 796. Nothing in the supplied region or history adds an ownership check at the switch boundary, so an operator removing/replacing the marker during the drain lets the switch proceed while the runner is unblocked (and the subsequent release can touch a marker this run no longer owns). This is a concrete gap in the intended 'hold is owned throughout the deploy' behavior, not merely a request for new scope; the serialization suggestion is extra, but the minimal recheck before the switch is an ordinary correctness repair.
